turns.prompt:
You are given one attached CSV file:
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal optics,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, select 5 candidates
that jointly span the best trade-off between a LARGE SHG tensor component
|d_ij| and a WIDE band gap. Neither is given for the pool. Your 5 picks are
scored by the dominated hypervolume they span in the normalized (|d_ij|,
band gap) plane, so a set of mutually non-dominated candidates covering the
frontier beats 5 candidates that are all strong on the same single axis.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the structures

**What controls the two axes**

* **Large |d_ij|** comes from (i) polarizable, covalent, easily-hybridized anions (I⁻ > Br⁻ > Se²⁻ > Cl⁻ > S²⁻), (ii) *stereochemically active lone pairs* (Ge²⁺, Sn²⁺, Sb³⁺, Tl⁺) or d¹⁰ cations (Cu⁺, Ag⁺, Hg²⁺, Cd²⁺) that give strongly anisotropic, aligned polyhedra, and (iii) a **polar** (non-centrosymmetric, non-cancelling) arrangement of those units.
* **Wide gap** comes from hard, ionic anions (Cl, F, O, S), closed-shell electropositive cations (Li, Mg, Al, Ba, Rb, Cs), and *absence* of Cu/Ag/Hg d-states or Te/I p-states at the band edges.
* These two requirements are antagonistic → the frontier is best sampled by a *chemically graded* series.

**Screening the pool**

* **c039 / c063 / c086 = RbGeI₃ / RbGeBr₃ / RbGeCl₃** — distorted, *polar* Ge(II) halide perovskites (checked: no inversion centre relating the four Ge sites). The Ge 4s² lone pair off-centres the GeX₃ pyramids coherently → this family is the classic "giant SHG" lone-pair system. The halogen substitution gives an almost ideal built-in trade-off: I (largest d, narrowest gap) → Br (intermediate) → Cl (moderate d, gap widened by ~1.5–2 eV). Three points on one Pareto staircase.
* **c080 = CsHg₄Ga₅Se₁₂** — polar Hg/Ga–Se framework of corner-shared tetrahedra, all apices aligned; Hg 5d/Se 4p edges give a mid gap (~2 eV class) with very large χ⁽²⁾ (Hg-chalcogenide NLO family). Independent chemistry insurance on the high-d side.
* **c053 = CdGa₂Cl₈** — non-centrosymmetric GaCl₄/Cd chloride: hard Cl ligands and no lone pair ⇒ small but finite d, while pushing the gap to the top of the pool. Anchors the wide-gap end of the frontier.
* Rejected: Cu/Ag/Te/Tl chalcogenides (c020, c047, c060, c069, c070, c073, c074, c038) — big d but gaps too small to help the frontier; centro/near-ionic salts (c023, c059, c061, c091, c007) — gap only, essentially zero d; SiC polytypes and Mg–Ga–Se / Li–Mg(Zn)–Ga–Se hypotheticals — respectable but interior to the staircase above; LiAlS₂ (c057) and ZnGa₂S₄ (c050) are good wide-gap sulfides but are largely dominated by RbGeCl₃ (similar gap, smaller d).

**Resulting frontier (schematic)**

| pick | expected gap | expected |d| | role |
|---|---|---|---|
| c039 RbGeI₃ | narrow | maximal | high-d anchor |
| c080 CsHg₄Ga₅Se₁₂ | narrow-mid | very large | high-d, different chemistry |
| c063 RbGeBr₃ | mid | large | best joint compromise |
| c086 RbGeCl₃ | wide | moderate | wide-gap + useful d |
| c053 CdGa₂Cl₈ | widest | small | wide-gap anchor |

These five are mutually non-dominated by construction (halide/chalcogenide polarizability graded monotonically against gap), so they should span a large dominated hypervolume rather than piling up on one axis.

**Final: c063, c039, c086, c080, c053**
